original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dline(m,n), the minimum number of distinct distances between a set of m points on a line and a set of n unrestricted points in the plane.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 18: determine the asymptotic value of the minimum number of distinct bipartite Euclidean distances between a set of m points contained in a line and a set of n unrestricted points in the real plane.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the intended open problem in the paper: it asks for an asymptotic formula for the minimum number of distinct distances when one point set has size m and lies on a line, while the other has size n and is otherwise unrestricted in the plane. That matches the one-restricted-set bipartite problem stated immediately before and in Problem 18 of Section 5. The only substantial issue is that your notation Dline(m,n) is not the paper’s own notation, and several paper-critical definitions are left implicit.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the real Euclidean plane R^2.
The quantity must be defined bipartitely: only distances ||p-q|| with p in the line-supported set and q in the unrestricted set are counted; distances within either set are irrelevant.
The minimization should be formalized over all pairs (P1,P2) with |P1|=m, |P2|=n, where P1 is contained in some line l in R^2 and P2 is an arbitrary finite subset of R^2.
The paper introduces the bipartite setup with the standing assumption m<=n without loss of generality; a stand-alone version should either include this assumption or note the symmetry.
The metric should be identified as the usual Euclidean distance.

It should be made explicit that no extra restriction is imposed on the unrestricted set P2; in particular, one should not add the separate additional hypothesis from Problem 19 that every line parallel or orthogonal to l contains a point of P2.
If you keep the notation Dline(m,n), it should be defined explicitly, since that symbol is not the paper’s displayed notation in the surrounding discussion.
refined_question: Let D_line(m,n) denote the minimum possible cardinality of {||p-q|| : p in P1, q in P2}, where P1,P2 are finite subsets of R^2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, P1 is contained in some line l in R^2, P2 is otherwise arbitrary, and only these cross-distances between P1 and P2 are counted. Assuming without loss of generality that m<=n, what is the asymptotic order of D_line(m,n) as a function of m and n?
justification: The draft targets the paragraph in Section 5 where the survey turns from unrestricted/unrestricted and curve/curve bipartite distance problems to the case in which exactly one set is restricted, namely a set on a line versus an unrestricted planar set; the immediately following open problem is Problem 18. The general bipartite notation D(P1,P2) and the standing assumption m<=n are introduced earlier in the same section, and those definitions are needed to make the question fully stand-alone. This is narrower than Problem 15 (both sets unrestricted), different from Problem 16 (both sets on lines), different from Problem 17 (both sets on algebraic curves), and different from Problem 19 (which adds an occupancy condition for lines parallel or orthogonal to the supporting line).
